title: A gate seal records where its command line came from at one of the five sites that open one, and a comment claims the parity it does not have
body:
## Summary

**A gate seal records where its command line came from at one of the five places devbin opens one, and a comment at the biggest gap claims the opposite.** `run_gate --source` is what puts the `from:` line in a seal, and `note_invocation` prints that line only when it is non-empty (`lib/runlog:391-392`, `[ -z "$source" ] || printf ... from: ...`). One caller passes it. So a person reading a seal for a command-level `run:` that went wrong sees the argv devbin ran and nothing at all about where that line was declared, which is the one thing the seal was opened to record.

Measured 2026-09-17 18:51Z at `169a349` (0082's commit), through the real dispatcher, in a project installed with `bin/devbin install --into <tmp> --force` holding `alpha.md`, `beta.md` and a dotfile `.hidden.md`, with the same command line declared twice -- once as an option, once as a command:

```yaml
commands:
  probe:
    options:
      gated:
        run: printf [%s]\n *.md
        grammar: generic
        log: GATED
  gatedcmd:
    run: printf [%s]\n *.md
    grammar: generic
    log: GATEDCMD
```

`devbin probe gated`, the seal at `tmp/probe/LATEST_GATED.out`:

```
devbin| invocation, one argument per line:
devbin|   platform: Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 / bash 5.3.20(1)-release
devbin|   run: 4aec367d
devbin|   from: config key commands.probe.options.gated.run, split into words by run_words, each a glob pattern (never eval'd)
devbin|   argv[0]: printf
devbin|   argv[1]: [%s]\n
devbin|   argv[2]: alpha.md
devbin|   argv[3]: beta.md
```

`devbin gatedcmd`, the seal at `tmp/gatedcmd/LATEST_GATEDCMD.out`, same words, same grammar, same project:

```
devbin| invocation, one argument per line:
devbin|   platform: Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 / bash 5.3.20(1)-release
devbin|   run: 652036af
devbin|   argv[0]: printf
devbin|   argv[1]: [%s]\n
devbin|   argv[2]: alpha.md
devbin|   argv[3]: beta.md
```

The second seal goes from `run:` straight to `argv[0]`. Nothing in it says a config key produced those words, which key it was, or that each word was a glob pattern matched at the project root -- and the words in it are the RESULT of that matching, so the declared line cannot be recovered by reading them.

## The population, since a count of one needs its denominator

Five calls open a gate in the runtime at `169a349`. One passes `--source`.

| Site                    | What it seals                                                     | Provenance in the seal |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `lib/resolve:772`       | an option's declared `run:`                                       | yes, at `lib/resolve:776` |
| `lib/resolve:906`       | a command's declared `run:`                                       | none                   |
| `lib/gatecmd:151`       | a catalogue option's command line (devbin's own data)             | none                   |
| `lib/gatecmd:134`       | a catalogue option implemented by a devbin function (`$fn`)       | none                   |
| `lib/cmd/fullcycle:770` | devbin's own `_fullcycle_run`                                     | none                   |

`--source` appears exactly once in the runtime: `lib/resolve:776`. The only other matches under `lib/` are `lib/runlog:1630` and `1634`, which are the flag's parser, ie the receiving end. `lib/cmd/check:250` is NOT in this table: it splits a catalogue line with `run_words` and runs it directly, inside a gate `run_builtin_gate` has already opened, so it adds no seal of its own.

The two sites that matter most are the two that run a line a PERSON declared: `lib/resolve:906`, and `lib/gatecmd:151` only to the extent that a project can reach devbin's catalogue. The other three run devbin's own code, where the provenance is still worth a line but nobody is going to be surprised by the answer.

## The comment that claims parity, which is the sharp end

`lib/resolve:894-896`, immediately above the command-level gate:

```
      # A command-level gate seals on exactly the terms an option-level one does
      # (D19), including the subshell at the project root -- it has to RETURN so
      # the seal gets written, so this is the one path here that does not exec.
```

It does not seal on exactly those terms, and **issue 0082 widened the difference** rather than creating it: 0082 improved the one `--source` string to name the glob rule, so the seal that has provenance now says more and the seal that has none still says nothing. A comment asserting a parity the code does not have is the defect class this project keeps filing, and it is the reason this is an issue rather than a nice-to-have.

## Shape of the fix

Pass `--source` at the four sites that do not, and say what each one is. The two declared sites want the config key, in the wording `lib/resolve:776` already uses. **The three devbin-owned sites want a phrase rather than a key, because none of them has one:** `lib/gatecmd` already builds exactly the right phrase for `run_words`'s refusal (`the catalogue's command line for '<cmd> <opt>'`), `lib/gatecmd:134` runs a function whose name is the honest answer, and `lib/cmd/fullcycle:770` runs devbin's own cycle. Then either make `lib/resolve:894-896`'s parity claim true or delete the claim; the fix makes it true, which is the better outcome for a comment that has already been wrong once.

## Not in scope

Deliberately fenced, on vc's instruction of 2026-09-17: this is provenance in the seal. It is not a redesign of `--source`, not a `from:` line for runs that open no gate, and not the `lib/runlog` parser. A further missing site belongs in this issue's record, not in a second fix.

## How it was found, and the sequencing

Found by dc on 2026-09-17 while reviewing 0082's documentation surfaces -- specifically while checking a claim dc had itself written down and not measured (that the command-level site "carries its own" banner). vc corrected the claim; measuring the correction is what produced the gap. Recorded because a wrong claim that gets measured is worth more than one that gets quietly fixed.

hv ruled on 2026-09-17 that this is filed as its own issue rather than folded into 0082, and closed out rather than parked. vc ruled the order: **filed and measured now, fixed after 0082 closes**, because the fix lands in `lib/resolve` and `lib/gatecmd`, which dc is reviewing for 0082, and a reviewer reading a file they have just rewritten is not a second pair of eyes.


## Fixed 2026-09-17 and 2026-09-18 -- every gate opener names where its command line came from, and the arms check the value (dc; reviewed by vc)

**Commits:** `76cb09d` (the six sites and the first four arms), `9689e0e` (the two site arms and the class arm rebuilt on `gate_spans`, after vc's review). The D19 comment's final wording is vc's, landed with 0087 at `860afd3`.

**What changed.** Five of the six calls that open a gate now pass `--source`. The sixth, an option's `run:` at `lib/resolve:772`, already did.

| Site                    | What its seal now says                                                            |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `lib/resolve` (command) | the same sentence as the option site, with this command's key                     |
| `lib/gatecmd` (line)    | the phrase `run_words` is already given for its refusal, naming the catalogue row |
| `lib/gatecmd` (builtin) | the function's name, and that there is no command line to look for                |
| `lib/cmd/fullcycle`     | devbin's own cycle, and that `_fullcycle_run` is a function in this process       |
| `bin/.devbin/cmd/test`  | devbin's own test handler, and that its command line is a literal, not config     |

The comment above the command-level gate at `lib/resolve` claimed it "seals on exactly the terms an option-level one does (D19)". It did not, and issue 0082 had widened the difference. It now says the parity was asserted twice while the code lacked it -- this issue's source line and 0087's wrapper flags -- and points at the arms that hold it, not at itself.

**THE SIXTH SITE WAS FOUND BY AN ARM, NOT BY READING.** This issue's own table said five openers, censused by reading every `run_gate` caller. The class arm named `bin/.devbin/cmd/test:30` the first time it ran: the census had read `lib/` and `bin/devbin` and stopped there.

**Arms, `tests/unit/runlog.bats`, six, each seen red first.**
- **The parity arm:** one command line declared twice, as a gated option and as a gated command, and the two seals' `from:` lines compared **with their keys removed**.
- A catalogue command line's gate names the catalogue, not a config key.
- A catalogue option that is a devbin function names the function.
- **Two site arms, added after review:** `lib/cmd/fullcycle` and `bin/.devbin/cmd/test` run for real through a `DEVBIN_LIB` shim whose runlog replaces `run_gate` with a stub printing the `--source` VALUE. The shim's helpers and config are the real ones, and nothing is cleaned, built or tested. Each asserts the value is non-empty AND names its own site.
- **The class arm:** every `run_gate` call in `lib/` and `bin/`, read through `gate_spans` (the one span reader, shared with 0087's arm), must carry a non-empty `--source`, and a call whose flags cannot be read is a finding. A floor fails it if the scan reads no call at all.

**WHAT EACH ARM KILLS, WHICH IS THE CORRECTION TO THIS SECTION'S FIRST DRAFT.** The first draft said the fullcycle and test-handler sites had no behavioural arm, "since driving either means running a full cycle, or the suite inside the suite", and that the class arm was their only cover. vc disproved the first half by driving both through the shim. The second half hid a hole: the class arm read the FLAG, not the value. Driven at the two devbin-owned scripts, three mutants per site:

| site        | line deleted          | `--source ""`        | the other site's sentence |
| ----------- | --------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `fullcycle` | site arm + class arm  | site arm (empty)     | site arm (wrong site)     |
| `test`      | site arm + class arm  | site arm (empty)     | site arm (wrong site)     |

Before the site arms, the last two columns survived everything. **The class arm's value check is a SUPPLEMENT, not the fix:** it reads the call's text, so it cannot see a value that is empty only at run time, or a site handed another site's sentence. **Its job is FINDING NEW SITES**, which is how it found the sixth.

**TWO SILENT DROPS IN THE SPAN READER, BOTH FIXED.** (1) The terminator was matched inside quoted text, and every source sentence in the runtime carries a `--` of its own, so spans closed at the sentence and never read the rest of the call. vc found this through 0087's floor, and `gate_spans` strips quoted text first. (2) An unterminated call -- no bare `--` -- was noticed only at the end of the file, so a second call below it was swallowed into one span and never read on its own. Control on the old reader: `lib/gatecmd`'s first call with its `--` removed AND its second call with `--source` deleted, and the class arm passed. `gate_spans` now also ends a span at the call's last line, and that pair is named: `:138` unterminated, `:159` no `--source`.

**Verified.**
- Red first, every arm, each at its own assertion. The class arm is red against `--source ""`, `''`, `--source=` with nothing, `--source` with no value, the line deleted, the unterminated pair above, and a tree with no `run_gate` caller.
- **The first round's six mutants** were built by exact-text substitution with **multi-line anchors, each unique in its file** -- the `--source` sentence alone is byte-identical at the two `lib/resolve` sites, so the anchors carried their surrounding lines. The parity mutant, which keeps the key and changes the terms, dies **only** at the parity arm.
- `runlog.bats` 91/0 and `dispatch.bats` 83/0 on the landed bytes, each on its own `TMPDIR`. No new shellcheck findings.

**Not covered, said rather than left.** The two `lib/resolve` sites and the two `lib/gatecmd` sites are held for their value by the parity and catalogue arms, and for the flag by the class arm. A seventh opener is held only by the class arm until someone writes its site arm, so it is checked for a non-empty literal, not for naming the right place.
